title: Add Version.is_compatible() to python-semver (upstream issue #284), contract resolved against upstream tests
import_hint: from semver import Version   (package lives in src/semver; the class is semver.version.Version)
statement: python-semver (src/semver, BSD-3) is a semantic-versioning library whose central class is semver.version.Version (also exported as semver.Version). Maintainers want a concise, readable way to ask 'is version y compatible with the version x that my code was written against?' (upstream issue #284). Add an instance method Version.is_compatible(other) -> bool to the Version class in src/semver/version.py. Semantics: the call `old.is_compatible(new)` returns True when `new` can be used in place of `old`. Two versions are compatible when their majors are equal, the minor of `new` is greater than or equal to the minor of `old`, and their prerelease parts are equal (both absent counts as equal). The patch part is ignored. Versions with major 0 are special: a major-0 version is compatible only with a version that is identical in major, minor, patch and prerelease. If `other` is not a Version (instances of Version subclasses are fine) raise TypeError with the message 'Expected a Version type but got <type of other>' (for example "Expected a Version type but got <class 'str'>"); the message must start with 'Expected a Version type ' followed by the words 'but got' and the type. Document the method with a docstring that includes at least two doctest examples. Do not change any other public behaviour, do not touch tests, docs or packaging files, and keep the whole existing pytest suite passing.
acceptance_criteria: Version(1, 2, 3).is_compatible(Version(1, 2, 3)) is True; Version(1, 2, 3).is_compatible(Version(1, 2, 4)) is True; Version(1, 2, 4).is_compatible(Version(1, 2, 3)) is True (patch is ignored).
Version(0, 1, 0).is_compatible(Version(0, 1, 0)) is True, but Version(0, 1, 0).is_compatible(Version(0, 1, 1)) is False (major 0 only matches an identical version).
Version(1, 1, 0).is_compatible(Version(1, 0, 0)) is False (lower minor); Version(2, 0, 0).is_compatible(Version(1, 5, 0)) is False (different major).

Version(1, 2, 3, 'rc.1').is_compatible(Version(1, 2, 3, 'rc.0')) is False; Version(1, 0, 0).is_compatible(Version(1, 0, 0, 'rc1')) is False; Version(1, 0, 0, 'rc1').is_compatible(Version(1, 0, 0)) is False (prerelease must be equal).

Version(1, 2, 3).is_compatible('wrongtype'), .is_compatible({'a': 2}) and .is_compatible([]) each raise TypeError whose message is 'Expected a Version type but got <class ...>' (starts with 'Expected a Version type but got').
A subclass instance is accepted: class CustomVersion(Version): pass; CustomVersion(1, 0, 0).is_compatible(Version(1, 0, 0)) is True.
The method's docstring contains doctest examples and the existing test suite (tests/) still passes.
contract_resolution: 2026-10-15: the first runs ended NEEDS HUMAN because the upstream held-out tests match the TypeError message with 'Expected a Version type .*'; the requester resolved the contract disagreement by specifying the exact upstream message.

upstream.reference: parent of PR #368 (upstream issue #284); the held-out tests are the pull request's own tests from merge commit 467ea0c7c198d60e0d88e32ee4d926b4e20eb74a
